solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hasty Scotch added to second round

parts.note: a lap is one round of a track
to scotch hopes is to dash them, to put an end to them

explanation.surface: Someone in a hurry pours a second round of whisky into the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like whisky but is the verb meaning to thwart; the charade runs S, LAP, then DASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe work done carelessly in a rush, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Small garment for baby, rather smart

parts.note: a nappy is a baby's diaper in British English

explanation.surface: A tiny baby outfit that looks quite stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: A NAPPY is the British word for a diaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Snappy describes clothing that is neat and stylish, so smart in that sense.

clue.text: One who likes a day on swamp and river

parts.note: mire is boggy ground, a swamp

explanation.surface: A nature lover spends a day at a marsh by the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who admires a thing regards it fondly, so is a person who likes it.

clue.text: Crime attractive? Individual's getting time inside

indicators.note: inside says the individual and time pieces sit within the attractive word

parts.note: dishy is British slang for good-looking
one's, the contraction of one is, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A handsome criminal is doing a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting time inside' suggests a jail term, but 'inside' is a container signal. DISHY is British slang for attractive.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonesty covers fraud and deceit, a broad category of wrongdoing.

clue.text: People waiting to receive this payment

definitions.text: People waiting to receive this payment

parts.words: People waiting to receive this payment
parts.note: people waiting suggests a queue, but it means restaurant waiters, who get a charge added to the bill

explanation.surface: A queue of people expecting to be paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waiting' means serving at table, not standing in line.
explanation.definitionFit: A restaurant adds this fee to the bill, nominally for the waiting staff.

clue.text: Recalled moment amidst endless leisure or vacation

indicators.note: amidst tells us the reversed moment sits in the middle of the other piece
endless says the final letter of the leisure word is dropped

parts.note: rest is leisure or time off

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the word for a moment is read backwards

parts.note: SEC is short for second, a moment

explanation.surface: A brief memory surfaces during an idle holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recalled' reverses the moment, 'endless' trims the leisure word, and 'amidst' sets one inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary or school break is called a recess, a period of holiday.

clue.text: Italian writer interrupted by first entry of his imitator

indicators.note: interrupted by means a letter breaks into the writer's name

parts.note: Umberto Eco was an Italian novelist

indicators.note: first entry of picks the opening letter of his

explanation.surface: An Italian author is cut off by the first appearance of his copycat.
explanation.walkthrough: Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose; H from 'his' goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo repeats back the sound made, so it mimics the speaker like an imitator.

clue.text: Summary chapter missing from very long book

indicators.note: missing from says the chapter letter is absent from the next word

parts.note: epic means very long, as in an epic journey
a tome is a large book

explanation.surface: A summary lacking a chapter from a huge book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing from' signals dropping the chapter letter from the 'very long' word before the book is added.
explanation.definitionFit: An epitome can mean an abstract or condensed account, so a summary.

clue.text: Broadcast equipment picked up line about 'Hot woman dancing '?

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the earlier pieces go round the hot letter

parts.note: to sow seed is to broadcast it

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means lifted, so the word reads upwards, in reverse

parts.note: rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A TV crew lifts its gear and lines up around a sizzling dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' means read upwards, so reversed; 'about' wraps everything before it round the hot letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A showgirl is a dancer in a revue or cabaret, a woman dancing on stage.

clue.text: Article by the writer is demonstrating intent

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
the writer refers to the setter as I, so the writer is becomes I'M

explanation.surface: A newspaper article written by the columnist shows what they set out to do.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords 'the writer' is the setter, I; with 'is' it gives I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim is a purpose or goal, the same as an intention or intent.

clue.text: Ostentatious transport that could provoke closet mirth

indicators.note: to provoke is to stir up, so the letters of the following words are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A flashy car so absurd it makes people laugh privately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could provoke' rearranges CLOSET MIRTH into the 11 letters of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An extended luxury car is a byword for showy travel, hence ostentatious transport.

clue.text: Fine enforcer ultimately wanted if car wrongly placed?

definitions.text: Fine enforcer ultimately wanted if car wrongly placed?

indicators.note: wrongly placed means put in the wrong order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of enforcer

explanation.surface: A parking official is needed if a car is badly parked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R from enforcer; with F and WANTED IF CAR, 'wrongly placed' rearranges the lot. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: This official issues fines to motorists who park illegally, enforcing parking rules.

clue.text: Police raid disrupted magazine

indicators.note: disrupted means thrown into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A police raid throws a magazine's office into chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: A magazine is a publication issued at regular intervals, a classic example of the term.

clue.text: It may be recalled as number penned by G&S?

definitions.text: It may be recalled as number penned by G&S?

indicators.note: recalled means called back, so the assembled letters are read in reverse
penned by means enclosed by, so the number abbreviation goes between the two letters

parts.note: the two initials G and S taken as letters

explanation.surface: A tune by Gilbert and Sullivan that people remember humming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'penned by' puts NO between G and S to make GNOS; 'may be recalled' reverses that. G&S are Gilbert and Sullivan, the Victorian comic opera writers.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical number is a piece to be sung, and Gilbert and Sullivan wrote many.

clue.text: People getting some education in Exeter or Warwick, say

parts.note: a race is a people or nation
a course is a unit of study

explanation.surface: Students taking classes at one of two English university towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Exeter and Warwick look like universities, but both towns have horse-racing tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter and Warwick both have tracks for horse racing, so they are examples.

clue.text: On radio, shout by cop with gun provides picture

indicators.note: on radio means heard over the air, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: an armed police officer shouts Freeze! meaning stand still

explanation.surface: A police radio broadcast of an armed officer's order.
explanation.walkthrough: The armed cop's shout is 'Freeze!'; 'On radio' tells you to take its sound, spelt differently.
explanation.definitionFit: A frieze is a decorative band of sculpture or painting along a wall, a kind of picture.

clue.text: One strolls along street dressed in mink, perhaps

indicators.note: dressed in says the street word is clothed by, i.e. placed inside, the fur

parts.note: mink is an example of fur
a lane is a narrow street

explanation.surface: A well-off person walks down the road wearing a mink coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dressed in' is a container signal. The answer is a French loan word for an idle man about town.
explanation.definitionFit: The French loan word names a leisurely stroller who idly wanders city streets.

clue.text: One put forward pressure to block Australian animals being imported into China

indicators.note: imported into means brought inside, so the inner pieces go within the china word

parts.note: china is rhyming slang for mate (china plate), i.e. pal

indicators.note: to block means to stop up, so the pressure letter plugs the animals

parts.note: roos is short for kangaroos
P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

explanation.surface: A trade suggestion about shipping kangaroos to China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to block' and 'being imported into' are two nested containers. China is Cockney rhyming slang: china plate = mate.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is an idea or plan put forward for consideration.

clue.text: Harm, etc, done in later encounter

indicators.note: done in the sense of done in, wrecked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Injuries and the rest sustained in a return fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'done' signals rearranging the letters of HARM ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: A rematch is a second contest between the same opponents, an encounter held later.

clue.text: Power to engage Bishop as man suitable for wedding

indicators.note: to engage means to take hold of, so the bishop letters are held inside

parts.note: might means power or strength
RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone with influence hires a bishop for a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop is styled Right Reverend, RR. 'engage' hints at betrothal too.
explanation.definitionFit: The ideal partner one hopes to marry is idiomatically called this.

clue.text: Sentimental place for Bishop, say, back in church cemetery finally

indicators.note: back means the word for a bishop's seat is written in reverse

parts.note: a bishop's see is the district under his authority

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of cemetery

explanation.surface: A soppy scene of a bishop in a church graveyard.
explanation.walkthrough: A bishop's seat is his see; 'back' reverses it, and 'finally' takes the last letter of cemetery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy describes something corny or mawkishly sentimental, an informal synonym.

clue.text: Boastful type very, very loud about the way things are done?

indicators.note: about means around, so the very pieces surround the manner word

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
how means the manner in which something happens
FF is fortissimo, very loud in music

explanation.surface: A loudmouth brags about how things should be done.
explanation.walkthrough: FF is the musical marking fortissimo; 'about' puts the two 'very' pieces round the manner word.
explanation.definitionFit: A show-off is a person who flaunts and brags, a boastful type.

clue.text: Charlie filling a post to gain promotion

indicators.note: filling means going inside, so the Charlie letter sits within the other piece

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it
C is Charlie in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A man named Charlie takes a job hoping to rise in rank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'filling a post' suggests a job, but 'filling' puts C inside A SEND.
explanation.definitionFit: To ascend is to rise, as a team does when it is moved up a league.

clue.text: Power and skill required for role

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for power
art is skill, as in the art of conversation

explanation.surface: An actor needs force and talent to land a role.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor's role is the part they play, a direct synonym.

clue.text: In our view adopting logic is subversive

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so the logic word goes inside the other piece

parts.note: to us means in our view, as in 'it seems to us'
reason is logic or rationality

explanation.surface: Someone declares a line of argument to be undermining the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' puts REASON inside TO US.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasonous acts betray and seek to overthrow the state, so they are subversive.

clue.text: Shock publicity event curtailed

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a stunt is something done for publicity

explanation.surface: An outrageous promotional event is cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' drops the final T from STUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to shock or stupefy someone, as a verb synonym.

clue.text: Expression of despair by pedestrian performer allowed no rehearsal?

parts.note: a sigh expresses despair
a treader is someone who treads, a walker or pedestrian

explanation.surface: A dull musician groans because there was no rehearsal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pedestrian' looks like an adjective meaning dull but is the noun for someone on foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A sight-reader plays music at first sight, so cryptically one who gets no rehearsal.

clue.text: Poetry regularly presented by soldier

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter of soldier

explanation.surface: Verses recited at intervals by a military man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: An ode is a lyric poem, so it is a piece of poetry.

clue.text: Fired by one unspecified prayer

parts.note: lit means set alight, fired
any means one of several, no particular one

explanation.surface: A person is sacked by some unnamed boss and starts praying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like dismissed but means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a series of petitions in church worship, a form of prayer.

clue.text: US agent pursuing European articles, having inadequate supply

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the agent comes after the articles

parts.note: UN is a French article and DER a German one
a fed is an FBI agent in American slang

explanation.surface: An American agent chases European goods and runs short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' looks like goods but means grammatical articles: French UN and German DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Underfed means given too little food, so lacking an adequate supply.
